submitted.rationale: Highest measured photocurrent (2.37 µA) of the three measurements. Photocurrent went up as the film became more Fe-rich and lower in V and Cr: 26 gave 0.46 µA, 35 gave 0.9 µA, 45 gave 2.37 µA. MEGNet gaps for the vanadate reference phase are 2.1–2.8 eV, close to the 2.72 eV illumination.

rejected.reason: 0.46 µA; V-rich film with more Cr performed worst

consultations.verdict: Weak support: MEGNet HSE gap 2.75 eV for mp-504509 (queried as a Fe-V-O vanadate reference) is near the 2.72 eV photon energy; FeVO4-type triclinic vanadates are known visible-absorbing photoanodes, so Fe:V≈1:1 with slight Cr alloying (index 35) is the prior best region. Model result is marginal/uninformative about the exact composition.

Uninformative-to-weak support: PBE gap 2.08 eV (HSE 2.75) for the reference vanadate means vanadate phases absorb near the 2.72 eV photon energy. The first point (35, near Fe:V 1:1) gave only 0.9 µA, so I'm exploring the V-rich region with mixed Cr/Fe (index 26), which is far from the first measurement.

Uninformative about composition: the SCAN gap of 2.80 eV confirms the vanadate gaps sit near the photon energy. The data show photocurrent falling as V goes up (35: 0.9 µA; 26, V-rich and more Cr: 0.46 µA), so I'm following the gradient toward Fe-rich, low-Cr composition 45.
